question:
Your yearbook team is using an AI to speed things up. It can save hours, but one of these steps can’t be left to the AI alone. Which one?

Steps:
1. Use the shape tool to mark 2 steps where an AI can safely help.
2. Use the arrow tool to point at the step where a human check matters most.
3. Use the text tool to write a one-sentence rule that starts “Before we print, a human checks...”
4. Record your voice explaining what would go wrong if that check were skipped.

rubric.description: No shape, arrow, or text is placed on the board, or the voice recording is missing or blank.
Student places shapes and an arrow, but types no rule.
Two shapes are on steps 1 and 2 (or either of them plus another reasonable step) AND the arrow points to step 3 AND the typed rule says a human checks the names before printing.
Meets all of the above AND the voice recording explains what goes wrong if step 3 is skipped (for example, 500 books with misspelled names) and why AI speed does not remove the need for the check.

whiteboard_starter_image_alt_text: "Making the school yearbook," shown as four numbered steps connected by arrows: 1, collect photos from students; 2, write a caption for each photo; 3, check that every name is spelled right; and 4, print 500 yearbooks.
